summary: Comprehensive: enumerates /agent/self for version + ACL default policy + gossip encryption + TLS min-version, catalog/services + catalog/nodes, and /v1/kv?recurse with secret-pattern scoring on both key and value. Distinguishes unauth-read vs auth-enforcing. Missing: no default-token guess (Consul doesn't ship default tokens but old bootstrap tokens are worth trying), no snapshot download probe (/v1/snapshot is a bbolt-equivalent full dump on Consul).

findings.tier_evidence: ACL default_policy != deny AND services/nodes/kv reads succeed = deterministic proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Also GET /v1/snapshot to pull the raft snapshot (contains ACL tokens hashed but readable KV+intentions). Then curl /v1/agent/token — writable token endpoints exist.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -s http://<ip>:8500/v1/kv/?recurse | jq -r '.[] | "\(.Key)=\(.Value|@base64d)"'; curl -s http://<ip>:8500/v1/snapshot -o consul.snap — then consul snapshot inspect.

findings.promotion_notes: Try token bruteforce is impractical (256-bit UUIDs). Instead try /v1/acl/bootstrap once — succeeds only if ACLs were enabled but never initialized (mirrors Nomad's pattern).
findings.tester_next_step: curl -X PUT http://<ip>:8500/v1/acl/bootstrap — if 200, JSON contains the initial management token (cluster-god); if 403 the system is already bootstrapped.

findings.tier_evidence: Actual base64-decoded KV values matched against private-key/AWS/JWT/DB-URI regexes and returned with a 120-byte preview — real credentials in hand.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed DB URIs into db/* modules and AWS keys into a metadata probe; wire into known_creds shared pool for cross-service reuse.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -s http://<ip>:8500/v1/kv/?recurse | jq -r '.[] | "\(.Key)|\(.Value|@base64d)"' | grep -Ei 'BEGIN.*PRIVATE|postgres://|AKIA|xox[abpr]-' — try each against its target service.

findings.tier_evidence: Absence of EncryptKey/SecretKey in DebugConfig via anon /agent/self is authoritative proof; passive read.
findings.promotion_notes: Send a crafted Serf join packet on 8301/UDP with no gossip key and confirm cluster membership acceptance — proves spoofing primitive.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -w gossip.pcap 'udp port 8301' — snoop membership; or use serf agent -join <ip>:8301 with no key to attempt cluster join.

findings.tier_evidence: Config disclosure of TLSMinVersion string only; no TLS handshake actually attempted with TLS 1.0.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually attempt a TLSv1.0 ClientHello against the port and confirm ServerHello negotiates it — deterministic probe.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect <ip>:8501 -tls1 -quiet — if handshake succeeds, TLS 1.0 is enabled on the wire.
